name: Walnut hallway unit

source.photo: reference photo (straight-on view of a floor-to-ceiling unit in a hallway alcove beside the entrance door, camera about mid-height; inside the cupboards, the drawer boxes and how the frame is fixed are not visible)
source.anchors: none given. 1000 W × 400 D × 2450 H assumed: the photo gives height ÷ width = 2.4, and at 1000 wide the counter lands at 852 mm, a normal console height. Depth 400 is assumed (shoes and coats need about that)
source.assumptions: Read from the photo against the assumed 1000 width: a black frame of 20 × 20 mm square steel tube (four posts standing on the floor, a ring of rails 20 mm off the floor and a second ring between the shoe cabinet and the drawers, which is the black line across the front); three walnut boxes sit between the posts and are screwed to them: a shoe cabinet (40–650), a drawer case with a 25 mm counter at 852 that overhangs the drawer fronts by 20, and an upper cupboard from 1600 to 2375. Between counter and cupboard: a lit bay on the left with no side panel (the wall shows between the posts), two shelves at equal spacing on steel brackets welded to the posts and a white back lit by LED profiles, and a coat bay on the right with a walnut back and three hooks at 1460. Upper cupboard: a cane door on the left (frame with rattan webbing in a groove), a door over a cupboard and an open bottle cubby above the shelf at 1932, an open niche round the electrical panel with no back so the panel stays reachable, and a small door on the right. Shoe-cabinet doors read as frame-and-panel with a lattice vent: built here in solid walnut (stiles 50, rails 35–50, stub mortise-and-tenon), four raised panels 15 mm and a 12 mm CNC fretwork panel, all floating in 6 mm grooves. Carcasses are 18 mm walnut-veneered MDF with ⌀8 dowels, 9 mm backs screwed on; drawer boxes 15 mm birch ply on 350 mm side-mount slides. Doors overlay on 35 mm cup hinges (half-overlay on the shared partition). Inferred, not in the photo: the steel rails behind the boxes, shelf brackets, all joinery, hinges, slides, drawer boxes, shoe shelves, the cupboard shelf, backs. The LED lighting needs a 24 V driver and must be wired by an electrician; keep the electrical panel accessible and do not enclose it

visible_in_photo: front rail between drawers and doors
inferred: steel rails behind and below the boxes

joinery.lit shelf → divider: dowel ×3; left end on welded bracket
